scenario_en: A disk-write budget holds 100 permits (1 permit = 1MB). One writer needs 60 permits and another needs 5; a finished 70MB write now returns 70 permits.
q: 释放时把 notify_all 换成 notify，会出什么问题？
q_en: What breaks if the release path calls notify instead of notify_all?
options: 可能只叫醒 5 许可那个，60 许可的写继续睡
所有等待线程照样都被叫醒，只是顺序变随机
归还的许可会被算错，available 加成两倍
被叫醒的线程会跳过 while 复查，直接扣减额度
options_en: It may wake only the 5-permit writer, leaving the 60-permit writer asleep.
Every waiting thread still wakes up; only the order becomes random.
The returned permits are miscounted and available is increased twice.
The woken thread skips the while re-check and deducts the budget anyway.
why: notify 只挑一个等待者，而等待者要的额度不同：被挑中的小写拿走额度后预算又变紧，大额度的写可能永远等不到自己那次唤醒。notify_all 让所有人复查，代价是惊群空醒。
why_en: notify wakes just one waiter, and since waiters need different amounts, the large writer can starve; notify_all makes everyone re-check at the cost of spurious wake-ups.
tradeoff: notify_all（人人复查，不漏掉大额度等待者）vs notify（唤醒少更省，但可能永远叫不到该醒的那个）

termDefinitions.meaning: 叫醒所有在这个条件变量上等待的线程，让它们各自重新检查条件是否满足。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: notify_all wakes every thread waiting on the condition variable so each one re-checks whether its condition now holds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次唤醒把大量线程同时叫起来抢同一份资源，多数复查失败后又睡回去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thundering herd is when one signal wakes many threads to contend for the same resource, and most re-check, fail, and go back to sleep.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个线程虽然一直在等，却因为调度或唤醒策略长期拿不到资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Starvation is when a thread waits indefinitely because the scheduling or wake-up policy keeps passing it over.

optionExplanations: 对，唤醒对象是任意一个，小写被叫醒拿走 5 许可后，大写这次机会就白白错过。
notify 的定义就是只叫醒一个等待者，不是把所有人叫醒后打乱顺序。
唤醒策略只影响叫谁起来，available += permits 这行算术完全不受影响。
复查逻辑写在 while 里，被叫醒的线程照样要过这道检查，不会跳过。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the wake target is arbitrary, so the small writer takes 5 permits and the big one loses its chance.
notify is defined as waking a single waiter, not waking everyone in shuffled order.
The wake policy only picks who gets up; the available += permits arithmetic is untouched.
The re-check lives in the while loop, so a woken thread still has to pass it.

scenario: 连接池报告 10 个连接全部 in use，但数据库那端吞吐极低。池里既有 1ms 跑完的快查询，也有占住连接 500ms 的分析查询。
scenario_en: A pool reports all 10 connections in use, yet database throughput is minimal; it mixes 1ms queries with analytics queries that hold a connection for 500ms.
q: 池显示满载但数据库很闲，最可能是什么状态？
q_en: The pool looks saturated but the database is idle — what state is the system actually in?
options: 连接被应用代码占着空转，in-use 不等于在干活
数据库正在主动限流，把大部分查询挡了回去
池容量设小了，把 10 调到 100 就能解决问题
池里的连接已经全部失效，握手失败发不出查询
options_en: The connections are checked out but idling in application code — in use is not the same as busy.
The database is throttling and rejecting most of the incoming queries.
The pool is undersized and simply raising it from 10 to 100 fixes it.
Every pooled connection has gone stale, so handshakes fail and no query is sent.
why: in-use 只说明连接被借走了，借走后线程可能在处理结果集或等别的 IO，数据库那一端是闲的。所以要看利用率而不是占用率，扩池只会把更多连接一起晾着。
why_en: In use only means the connection is checked out; the borrowing thread may be chewing on results, so measure utilisation rather than occupancy.
tradeoff: 看占用率（好采集，但会把空转当成满载）vs 看数据库侧吞吐与利用率（更真实，但要额外埋点）

termDefinitions.meaning: 资源真正在做有效工作的时间占比，区别于只是被谁借走的占用率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Utilisation is the share of time a resource spends doing useful work, as opposed to merely being checked out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 池里那些已被数据库或网络单方面关掉、但池还以为可用的连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stale connection is one the database or network already closed while the pool still believes it is usable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端主动拒绝或延迟超出配额的请求，用来保护自己不被压垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throttling is a server deliberately rejecting or delaying requests beyond a quota to protect itself from overload.

optionExplanations: 对，10 条里多数只是被借着，线程在处理结果集，数据库端并没有活要干。
限流会让查询返回错误或明显变慢，而这里症状是数据库端根本收不到请求。
连接空转时扩池只是让更多连接一起闲着，还多占数据库内存和描述符。
连接失效会表现为借出后报错或重连，而不是安静地一直显示为使用中。
optionExplanations_en: Right — most of the ten are merely borrowed while threads chew on results, so the database has nothing to do.
Throttling would surface as errors or clear slowdowns, but here the database sees almost no requests at all.
Growing the pool while connections idle just parks more of them, costing extra database memory and descriptors.
Stale connections show up as errors or reconnects on checkout, not as quietly in-use connections.

scenario: 10 连接的池被所有租户共用。一个批量导数租户长期把池占满，交互式租户的请求排在后面，多数等到超时。
scenario_en: One 10-connection pool is shared by all tenants; a bulk-import tenant keeps it saturated and interactive tenants queue behind it until they time out.
q: 怎么改才能让交互式租户不被批量租户长期饿死？
q_en: How do you keep interactive tenants from being starved by the bulk tenant?
options: 按租户或优先级把池切成几份，各自有配额
把池换成严格公平队列，按到达顺序发放连接
把池容量从 10 调到 100，让大家都能拿到
去掉获取超时，让交互式请求一直等到有连接
options_en: Partition the pool by tenant or priority so each class gets its own quota.
Switch to a strictly fair queue that hands out connections in arrival order.
Raise the pool from 10 to 100 connections so everyone can get one.
Drop the acquire timeout so interactive requests wait until a connection frees up.
why: 竞争压垮吞吐时，公平只保证排队顺序，救不了大户长期霸占容量；按租户分区让每类请求有各自的额度。代价是分区之间的空闲额度不能互相借用。
why_en: Fairness only fixes ordering, not a tenant that holds capacity for long stretches, so partition the pool per tenant at the cost of stranded idle capacity.
whenOtherWins: 如果各租户负载相近、只是偶尔有人排在后面，严格公平 FIFO 更简单，不用给每个分区单独调容量。
tradeoff: 按租户分区（防饿死，但空闲额度不共享）vs 单一共享池（利用率高，但大户能长期占满）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一份共享资源拆成若干独立配额，各自只能用自己那份，互不挤占。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioning splits one shared resource into separate quotas so each class can only consume its own share.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：等待者严格按到达顺序被服务，不允许插队。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FIFO, or First In First Out, serves waiters strictly in the order they arrived.

termDefinitions.meaning: 等资源的时间上限，超过就放弃并向上返回失败，而不是继续挂着。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An acquire timeout caps how long a thread waits for a resource before giving up and returning an error.

optionExplanations: 对，交互式租户有专属的那几条连接，批量任务再忙也吃不到这部分额度。
公平只解决“谁先排上”，批量租户仍会一轮一轮把连接全借走。
扩容让批量任务跑得更凶，数据库内存和描述符先扛不住，比例问题没变。
去掉超时只会把请求线程一起耗尽，用户看到的还是超时，只是更晚。
optionExplanations_en: Right — interactive tenants own a slice of connections that the bulk job can never take.
Fairness only decides who queues first; the bulk tenant still takes every connection round after round.
More connections just let the bulk job run harder while the database runs out of memory and descriptors.
Removing the timeout only exhausts request threads too; users still see timeouts, just later.

scenario: 限并发的代码不加锁：先读 active < 5 判断有没有余量，再执行 active += 1。5 个线程几乎同时到达，都读到 active = 4。
scenario_en: Concurrency limiting code checks active < 5 and then does active += 1 without a lock; five threads arrive together and all read active = 4.
q: 这种 check-then-act 会把系统带到什么状态？
q_en: What state does this check-then-act pattern leave the system in?
options: 五个线程都通过检查，active 冲到 9 超出限额
五个线程全被拒绝，因为读到的值已经过期作废
active 会被减成负数，计数器从此永久损坏
结果仍然正确，只是有些线程要多等一两轮调度才能通过
options_en: All five pass the check and active climbs to 9, above the limit.
All five are rejected because the value they read is already stale.
active is decremented below zero and the counter is permanently corrupted.
The result stays correct; some threads merely wait an extra scheduling round or two.
why: 读和写之间没有锁，5 个线程都基于同一个 4 各加一，上限 5 被冲到 9，下游实际收到 9 路并发就是超载。修法是用 semaphore 的 acquire 把检查和占用做成一个原子动作。
why_en: With no lock between the read and the write, all five threads act on the same stale 4 and push concurrency to 9, so use a semaphore acquire to make check and take atomic.
tradeoff: semaphore 原子 acquire（检查与占用不可分割）vs 裸计数器 check-then-act（代码直观，但限额形同虚设）

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读共享状态做判断、再基于判断修改它；两步之间没有锁的话，状态可能已被别人改掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Check-then-act reads shared state, decides, then mutates it; without a lock in between, the state can change between the two steps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对外表现为不可分割的一步，其他线程看不到它的中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic operation appears indivisible to other threads, which never observe an intermediate state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个许可计数器限制同时能进入某段代码的线程数：acquire 减一、release 加一，计数为零时下一个 acquire 阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A semaphore is a permit counter that caps how many threads run a section at once; acquire decrements it, release increments it, and the next acquire blocks at zero.

optionExplanations: 对，每个线程都拿着自己那份过期的 4 做判断，五次自增全部生效，限额被静默突破。
过期的值不会自动作废，代码照样当真，判断结果是“还有余量”而不是拒绝。
这里只有自增没有配对的自减，计数只会偏大，不会掉到负数。
调度顺序不同只让超限出现得或早或晚，缺锁这件事本身不会被调度修好。
optionExplanations_en: Right — each thread decides on its own stale 4, all five increments land, and the cap is silently breached.
A stale value is not invalidated automatically; the code trusts it and concludes there is room.
There is only an increment here with no paired decrement, so the count skews high, never negative.
Different scheduling only changes when the overshoot appears; it cannot repair the missing lock.

scenario: 图片处理用 5 许可的信号量限并发。上游 HTTP 客户端 2 秒就超时，但高峰期请求线程挂在 acquire 上一直不返回。
scenario_en: Image processing caps concurrency with a 5-permit semaphore; the upstream HTTP client times out after 2 seconds, yet request threads hang forever inside acquire.
q: 信号量这一侧该怎么改，才不会让请求线程永久阻塞？
q_en: What change on the semaphore side stops request threads from blocking forever?
options: 改用 tryAcquire(timeout)，等不到就返回失败
把许可数从 5 加到 50，降低线程阻塞的概率
改用队列的 poll(timeout)，因为信号量没有超时变体
在 acquire 外面套一层重试循环，直到拿到许可为止
options_en: Use tryAcquire with a timeout and fail when no permit arrives in time.
Raise the permits from 5 to 50 so threads are less likely to block.
Use the queue's poll with a timeout, since semaphores have no timed variant.
Wrap acquire in a retry loop that keeps trying until a permit is obtained.
why: 阻塞版 acquire 会一直等下去，请求线程被耗光；tryAcquire(timeout) 在窗口内拿不到就返回 false，调用方可以回 503。代价是高峰期会主动丢掉一些本可成功的请求。
why_en: A plain acquire waits indefinitely and drains the request threads, while tryAcquire with a timeout fails fast so the caller can return a 503.
whenOtherWins: 后台批处理没有用户在等响应时，阻塞版 acquire 更简单：让任务排队比直接丢弃它更划算。
tradeoff: tryAcquire(timeout) 快速失败（保住线程，但会误杀请求）vs acquire 无限等待（不丢请求，但线程会被耗光）

termDefinitions.meaning: 信号量的限时获取：在给定时间内拿到许可就返回真，超时则返回假而不是继续等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: tryAcquire with a timeout returns true if a permit arrives within the window and false when it expires, instead of waiting on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 阻塞队列的限时取元素：等到超时还没有元素就放弃，返回空值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: poll with a timeout takes an item from a blocking queue but gives up and returns empty once the timeout expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 状态码 Service Unavailable，告诉调用方服务当前没有容量、可以稍后重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable tells the caller the service currently has no capacity and the request may be retried later.

optionExplanations: 对，超时窗口设在客户端 2 秒之内，线程能及时脱身并把过载变成明确错误。
加许可只是把过载放行到下游，CPU 打满之后线程照样堆在那里等。
信号量本身就有 tryAcquire 的限时变体，不必为了超时改造成队列。
重试循环等价于换个写法的无限等待，线程一样回不来，还多烧 CPU。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a timeout inside the client's 2 seconds lets the thread escape and turns overload into an explicit error.
More permits just admit the overload downstream; once the CPU saturates, threads pile up again.
Semaphores already offer a timed tryAcquire, so there is no need to convert this into a queue.
A retry loop is unbounded waiting in disguise: the thread still never returns and burns CPU.

scenario: 磁盘写预算 100 许可、1 许可 = 1MB，代码算 permits = max(1, ceil(字节数/MB))。这台服务上大量写入只有 4KB。
scenario_en: A disk-write budget has 100 permits at 1MB each, computing permits = max(1, ceil(bytes/MB)); most writes on this service are only 4KB.
q: 如果去掉 max(1, ...) 这层地板，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the max(1, ...) floor is removed from the permit calculation?
options: 4KB 的写各算 0 个许可，可无限并发绕过预算
4KB 的写会被向上并成 1MB，预算反而算得偏多
可用许可会被减成负数，之后的写永远拿不到许可
大写入会拿不到许可，因为小写入先把额度全抢走了
options_en: Each 4KB write costs 0 permits and unlimited tiny writes bypass the budget.
Each 4KB write rounds up to 1MB, so the budget is over-counted instead.
Available permits go negative and later writes can never acquire again.
Large writes starve because the small writes grabbed all the budget first.
why: 不设地板时 4KB 除以 1MB 取整就是 0，这些写既不减预算也不用等，几千个可以同时压到磁盘上，限流对最常见的负载完全失效。地板 1 保证每次写至少记一笔账。
why_en: Without the floor a 4KB write rounds to zero permits, so it neither consumes budget nor waits, and thousands can hit the disk at once.
tradeoff: 地板 1 许可（小写也记账，但对 4KB 明显高估）vs 按真实比例计（更精确，但 0 许可等于不限流）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不满一个单位的余数也算作一个单位，例如 1.1MB 按 2MB 计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ceiling rounds any partial unit up to a whole one, so 1.1MB is charged as 2MB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预算的最小记账单位，这里一个许可代表 1MB 在途数据，拿走就减、归还就加。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A permit is the unit of budget accounting; here one permit stands for 1MB of in-flight data, decremented on acquire and restored on release.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经开始但还没完成的操作正占用的数据量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-flight data is the amount held by operations that have started but not yet finished.

optionExplanations: 对，占 0 个许可的写永远满足条件，while 循环一次都不会挡住它们。
并成 1MB 正是保留地板后的行为，去掉它得到的是 0 而不是 1。
扣减 0 不会改变计数，可用许可停在原地，不存在被减成负数一说。
小写入压根不占额度，也就谈不上把大写入的额度抢走。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a write costing zero permits always satisfies the condition, so the while loop never blocks it.
Rounding up to 1MB is exactly what keeping the floor does; removing it yields 0, not 1.
Subtracting zero leaves the counter unchanged, so it never drifts below zero.
Tiny writes consume no budget at all, so they cannot take anything away from large ones.

scenario: 磁盘写预算 100 许可，1 许可 = 1MB，permits = ceil(字节数 / 1MB)。实际负载里有不少 1.1MB 这种刚过整数的文件。
scenario_en: A disk-write budget holds 100 permits at 1MB each with permits = ceil(bytes / 1MB), and the real workload contains many files just over a whole megabyte, like 1.1MB.
q: 这种向上取整的许可粒度带来什么后果？
q_en: What is the consequence of this ceiling-based permit granularity?
options: 多记的零头累积，真实在途约 98MB 就开始阻塞
少记的零头累积，真实在途悄悄超过 100MB 才阻塞
取整只影响统计口径，阻塞时刻仍精确卡在 100MB
取整会让大文件优先被调度，1.1MB 的文件排到最后
options_en: The over-charged remainders add up, so writes start blocking around 98MB of real data.
The under-charged remainders add up, so real in-flight data quietly exceeds 100MB.
Rounding only affects reporting; blocking still happens exactly at 100MB.
Rounding prioritises large files and pushes 1.1MB files to the back of the queue.
why: 许可数 = ceil(字节数 / 1MB)，MB 是 1024×1024 字节；1.1MB 记 2 个许可，多记的零头累积后真实在途约 98MB 就用光 100 许可。这个 100 是保守上界，用来定阻塞点，不是精确在途量。
why_en: Permits equal the byte count divided by one megabyte rounded up, so a 1.1MB file is charged 2 and blocking kicks in near 98MB of real data — a deliberately conservative bound.
tradeoff: 整数许可粒度（实现简单，只做加减法）vs 按字节精确记账（预算准，但计数更细、竞争更多）

termDefinitions.meaning: 兆字节，这里按 1024×1024 = 1048576 字节计，是许可的换算单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MB, or megabyte, is taken here as 1024 by 1024 bytes and is the conversion unit for one permit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不满一个单位的余数也算作一个单位，例如 1.1MB 按 2MB 计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ceiling rounds any partial unit up to a whole one, so 1.1MB is charged as 2MB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 故意估得比真实值大一点的限额，宁可提前挡住也不愿超出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conservative bound deliberately over-estimates usage so the system blocks early rather than overshooting.

optionExplanations: 对，2 个许可只装 1.1MB 真数据，约 50 个文件就用完 100 许可，阻塞点提前到 98MB 左右。
取整方向反了：ceil 只会多记不会少记，所以真实在途永远小于等于许可数。
记账单位是整数许可，1.1MB 记 2 个的那 0.9MB 差额是真实存在的，不只是报表口径。
许可只决定谁能开始写，不排序也不区分文件大小，先到的先拿。
optionExplanations_en: Right — two permits cover only 1.1MB of real data, so about 50 files exhaust 100 permits near 98MB.
The rounding goes the other way: ceil only over-charges, so real in-flight data never exceeds the permit count.
Accounting happens in whole permits, so the 0.9MB charged beyond a 1.1MB file is a real gap, not a reporting artifact.
Permits only decide who may start writing; they impose no ordering and no preference by file size.

scenario: 10 连接的池已被借空，第 11 个线程调 queue.get() 等连接。这台机器在 3 万 QPS 下 CPU 已经吃紧。
scenario_en: All 10 pooled connections are checked out and an eleventh thread calls queue.get(); the box is already CPU-bound at 30k QPS.
q: 这个线程在等待期间对 CPU 做了什么？
q_en: What does that waiting thread do to the CPU while it waits?
options: 被 OS 挂起，不占 CPU，归还连接时再被唤醒
在循环里反复检查队列是否非空，占满一个核心
每隔 10ms sleep 一次再查一遍，延迟取决于间隔
立刻返回空值，由调用方自己决定什么时候重试
options_en: It is suspended by the OS, uses no CPU, and is woken when a connection returns.
It spins in a loop checking whether the queue is non-empty, pinning one core.
It sleeps 10ms and polls again, so latency depends on the polling interval.
It returns empty immediately and leaves the caller to decide when to retry.
why: 阻塞队列的 get 走 OS 的挂起唤醒原语：线程让出 CPU，直到 put 把它叫醒。这正是选阻塞队列而不是自旋或 sleep 轮询的效率理由，代价是唤醒要过一次调度延迟。
why_en: A blocking queue's get uses OS suspend and wake primitives, so the thread yields the CPU until a put wakes it, at the price of one scheduling delay.
tradeoff: OS 挂起唤醒（等待期间零 CPU，但唤醒有调度延迟）vs 自旋或轮询（反应更快，但持续烧 CPU 或引入固定间隔）

termDefinitions.meaning: 取元素时如果队列为空会让线程等待，同时充当可用对象集合和等待机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blocking queue makes a take wait while it is empty, serving as both the pool of available objects and the waiting mechanism.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线程在循环里不停重读条件，不释放 CPU，等待期间一直烧一个核。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Spin-waiting keeps re-reading a condition in a loop without yielding, burning a core for the whole wait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量服务每秒处理多少请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, or Queries Per Second, measures how many requests a service handles each second.

optionExplanations: 对，线程进入内核的等待队列，直到有人 put 才被调度回来，期间不消耗 CPU。
自旋在 3 万 QPS 这种场景下会把本就紧张的核心烧掉，队列并没有这么实现。
sleep 轮询会带来最多一个间隔的额外延迟，也没必要——队列自己会精确唤醒。
立刻返回是不带超时的 poll 语义，get 的默认行为是等下去而不是放弃。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the thread parks in a kernel wait queue and is rescheduled only when someone puts a connection back.
Spinning would burn an already scarce core at 30k QPS, and that is not how the queue is implemented.
Sleep-and-poll adds up to one interval of extra latency and is unnecessary since the queue wakes precisely.
Returning immediately is the semantics of a non-blocking poll; get waits by default rather than giving up.

scenario: 低层设计面里你说“用 5 许可的信号量限制并发下载”，面试官追问：它到底是怎么把线程阻塞住的？
scenario_en: In a low-level design round you say you'll cap downloads with a 5-permit semaphore, and the interviewer asks how it actually blocks a thread.
q: 面对这个追问，最稳的回答策略是什么？
q_en: What is the safest way to answer that follow-up?
options: 说它用 OS 原语挂起和唤醒线程，标准库已实现
现场手写一个基于自旋锁的信号量内部实现给他看
承认不清楚，改口说不用信号量，换成加锁计数器
说它内部就是一个 while 循环，不停地检查计数器
options_en: Say it uses OS primitives to park and wake threads, and the standard library handles that.
Whiteboard your own spin-lock-based implementation of a semaphore on the spot.
Admit you don't know and switch to a lock-protected counter instead.
Say that internally it is just a while loop constantly re-checking the counter.
why: 这类追问考的是你知不知道抽象边界：讲清 acquire/release 的语义，加一句挂起唤醒由 OS 做就够了。硬讲内部容易讲错，还会把话题从设计带偏到实现。
why_en: The follow-up tests whether you know the abstraction boundary, so state the acquire and release semantics plus OS park and wake, and leave the internals to the library.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮明确是操作系统或并发原语实现岗，面试官要的就是内部结构，那才该展开等待队列的细节。
tradeoff: 答 API 语义（聚焦设计判断，稳）vs 答内部实现（显得深入，但容易讲错且偏题）

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作系统提供的底层机制，这里指把线程挂起进等待队列、有事件时再唤醒的调度能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An OS primitive is a low-level kernel facility, here the ability to park a thread in a wait queue and wake it when an event occurs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拿不到锁就在循环里反复重试的锁，等待期间不让出 CPU。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A spin lock retries in a tight loop when the lock is unavailable, never yielding the CPU while it waits.

termDefinitions.meaning: 你负责说清语义、把实现交给底层库的那条线，答题时要主动点明它在哪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstraction boundary is the line where you own the semantics and the library owns the implementation.

optionExplanations: 对，一句“挂起唤醒由 OS 做，Java 的 Semaphore 已经封装好”就答到位了。
手写内部实现风险高：写错一处就变成考实现细节，设计讨论也被打断。
追问实现不等于方案有问题，换掉信号量反而暴露对工具的不自信。
说成 while 循环等于把它讲成自旋忙等，与真实的挂起唤醒语义相反。
optionExplanations_en: Right — saying the OS parks and wakes threads and Java's Semaphore wraps that is a complete answer.
Writing the internals live is risky: one slip turns the round into an implementation quiz and derails the design talk.
A follow-up about internals is not a sign the design is wrong; swapping the tool signals low confidence.
Describing it as a while loop turns it into busy-waiting, the opposite of real park-and-wake semantics.

scenario: 服务每秒 1000 个请求，每个请求都要查一次数据库。有人提议每来一个请求就现开一条连接、用完关掉。
scenario_en: A service takes 1,000 requests per second and each one queries the database; someone proposes opening a fresh connection per request and closing it after.
q: 哪些代价说明数据库连接必须池化复用？（多选）
q_en: Which costs explain why database connections must be pooled and reused? (multi-select)
options: 每条连接都占数据库服务端的一块内存
每条连接占一个文件描述符，OS 有硬上限
建立连接要走一次握手，耗时加在每个请求上
连接对象是无状态的，复用能省掉序列化开销
options_en: Every connection consumes memory on the database server.
Every connection holds a file descriptor, and the OS caps how many exist.
Establishing a connection costs a handshake, added to every single request.
Connections are stateless objects, so reusing them saves serialization work.
why: 连接贵在三处：数据库端内存、文件描述符、握手耗时。1000 QPS 下每请求新建等于把这三笔成本乘一千；池化把它们摊到启动那一次，代价是并发被池容量卡住。
why_en: Connections are expensive in three ways — server memory, file descriptors, and handshake time — so pooling pays those costs once at startup and caps concurrency instead.
tradeoff: 池化复用（摊掉建连成本，但并发被池容量卡死）vs 每请求新建（并发不受限，但内存、描述符和握手全线爆炸）

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作系统给每个打开的文件或套接字分配的整数句柄，每个进程能同时持有的数量有上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A file descriptor is the integer handle the OS assigns to each open file or socket, and each process can hold only a limited number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 建连时的往返协商过程，包含网络往返和认证，耗时通常是毫秒级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A handshake is the round-trip negotiation that sets up a connection, including network round trips and authentication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不保存任何跨调用的上下文；数据库连接恰恰相反，它带着套接字、认证和事务状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stateless means keeping no context between calls, which a database connection is not: it carries a socket, credentials, and transaction state.

optionExplanations: 是，每条连接在数据库进程里都有会话缓冲区，连接一多先压垮的是数据库内存。
是，描述符用尽后整个进程连新文件都打不开，故障范围远超数据库这条路径。
是，握手的毫秒级往返直接叠进每个请求延迟，1000 QPS 下这笔账最刺眼。
不是，连接恰恰有状态：套接字、凭据、事务上下文都挂在上面，正因如此才要复用。
optionExplanations_en: Yes — each connection keeps session buffers inside the database process, so memory there is the first thing to break.
Yes — once descriptors run out the whole process cannot open new files, so the blast radius exceeds the database path.
Yes — the millisecond handshake round trip lands directly in every request's latency, which hurts most at 1,000 QPS.
No — connections are stateful, carrying a socket, credentials, and transaction context, which is exactly why they are reused.
